title: Traumatic brain injury and concussion in the hospital
question: From this hospital discharge summary, assign the ICD-10-CM code for the head injury (only that code).
note:
Admission Date: 05/12/2026
Discharge Date: 05/13/2026
Reason for Admission: Evaluation of concussion after fall.

Vitals:
BP: 132/78
HR: 74 (RRR)
Temp: 98.6 F
SpO2: 97% on RA

Labs:
WBC: 8.2
Hgb: 14.1
Plt: 210k
Na: 139
K: 4.0
Creatinine: 1.1 (eGFR: 72)

Review of Systems:
Pt c/o headache and mild dizziness following fall. Denies nausea, vomiting, vision changes, or focal weakness. No confusion noted.

Social History:
Lives with wife in private residence. Retired. Non-smoker.

Family History:
Father: HTN. Mother: Type 2 DM.

Hospital Course:
Pt is an 85-year-old male admitted for overnight observation following a fall at home. Pt was unconscious for about 5 minutes. Initial neuro exam showed mild somnolence but pt was alert and oriented to person, place, and time by admission. CT head and MRI brain were both normal. No acute changes noted during observation. Pt remained stable throughout the stay. Neuro checks were WNL. Pt voiced no new complaints and was cleared for discharge to home with safety precautions.

Discharge Diagnoses:
Concussion

Discharge Medications:
Acetaminophen 500mg BID PRN for headache.

Follow-up:
Pt to f/u with PCP in 1 week for routine check.

Electronically signed,
A. Rivera, MD
05/13/2026
explanations: Concussion with loss of consciousness of 30 minutes or less, initial encounter: S06.0X1A (no HCC).

distractors.why: A concussion is documented with normal imaging, not a diffuse injury.

style.document: Write a hospital discharge summary with sections: Admission Date, Discharge Date, Reason for Admission, Hospital Course, Discharge Diagnoses, Discharge Medications, Follow-up. It is the inpatient record of this hospital stay, not an office note.
